title: Runtime Integrated Experimentation Playbook
author: Evan Garcia
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the integrated experimentation framework used by the runtime, kernel scheduling, profiling, and benchmarking teams to design, run, and validate production-impacting experiments. It codifies an observability-first approach that ties kernel and scheduler changes to measurable signals (latency, cost, kv-cache health, queueing) and defines guardrails for safe rollout across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments.

Goals and scope:
- Enable low-risk kernel and scheduler experiments that yield reproducible performance and cost delta measurements.
- Provide a single source of truth for experiment lifecycle: design, stage validation, canary rollouts, full rollout, and rollback.
- Ensure experiments are observable end-to-end and tied to SLO and cost budgets.
- Apply to changes affecting: kernel selection logic, batch slicing, preemption policies, KV cache heuristics, quantized execution paths, and routing/fallback rules.

Owners and roles:
- Experiment Lead: owner of the change (usually runtime or kernel eng).
- Instrumentation Lead: observability or profiling owner responsible for telemetry coverage.
- Benchmarks Owner: benchmarking team contact who runs controlled traffic and cost simulations.
- SRE Reviewer: approves rollout policy and SLA gating.
- Oncall rotation: runtime-oncall for the day of canary and 24h after full rollout.

Required telemetry and dashboards (minimum coverage):
- request.timeline.kernel_exec_ms (histogram)
- request.queue.wait_ms (histogram)
- kernel.dispatch.queue_depth (gauge)
- gpu.occupancy.percent (gauge)
- kvcache.hit_rate.prefix (ratio)
- tokens.per_request (summary)
- per_token_cost_usd (derived counter)
- request.error_rate (rate)
- model.variant.fallback_rate (rate)
- cpu_p95_sys/user_ms (histogram)
- p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, p999_latency_ms (quantiles)

SLOs and experimental thresholds (example):
- Production latency SLO: p99 < 300ms for text-generation small models (configurable per model family).
- Error budget: no more than 1% of p99 variance attributable to experiment in the first 24 hours.
- Cost target: measured per-token cost delta must be within +/- 5% of predicted.
- Fallback bound: model variant fallback rate must not exceed 0.1% during canary.

Experiment lifecycle checklist:
1) Proposal and hypothesis
   - Document hypothesis (what change, why, expected delta on latency/cost).
   - Include experiment lead, reviewers, and owners in doc metadata.
   - Define success criteria in both statistical and operational terms.
2) Instrumentation and smoke tests (pre-merge)
   - Add telemetry points and expose counts/metrics as above.
   - Local microbench smoke runs must pass (no new failures).
   - Add unit tests for kernel selection edge-cases.
3) Synthetic benchmark / offline validation
   - Run microbench suite mirroring representative sequence-length distributions.
   - Produce delta report: p50/p95/p99, throughput, GPU occupancy, and token cost estimate.
   - Benchmarks Owner signs off on data quality.
4) Staging canary (internal traffic)
   - Deploy to isolated staging pool (10% of staging capacity).
   - Run the system for 24-72 hours with synthetic replay and limited real traffic.
   - Monitor the experiment dashboard and Slack alert channel.
   - Abort if: error rate increases > 0.05 absolute, fallback rate > 0.2%, or p99 increases > 50ms above baseline.
5) Production canary (small customer/region)
   - Gradually enable 1% -> 5% -> 20% traffic over 6–24 hours with verification at each step.
   - Post-step checks: run automated smoke suite, compare telemetry windows (30min, 3h, 24h).
   - Require manual approval from SRE Reviewer before entering >20% traffic.
6) Full rollout and post-rollout validation
   - Proceed if all gating checks pass for 24h at 20% traffic.
   - Monitor error budget burn, cost prediction, and fallback behaviors for 72h.
   - Complete rollout only after Benchmarks Owner and SRE Reviewer sign-off.
7) Postmortem and learnings
   - Capture results in the experiment page: data, dashboards, replay tokens, and decision rationale.
   - If rollout fails, follow the rollback playbook (see section below).

Gating criteria (explicit):
- Safety gates (fail fast): request.error_rate increase > 0.05 absolute, p99 increase > 2x baseline for more than 10 minutes, queue_depth sustained increase > 3x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Quality gates (manual): fallbacks above target, increased hallucination rate on eval prompts (if applicable), or new error classes.
- Cost gates: per-token cost regression > +10% (auto pause) or > +5% requiring manual approval.

Rollback and mitigation steps (runbook):
Immediate actions (first 15 minutes):
1) Pause the experiment via feature-flag:  featurectl set kernel_experiment=false --env=prod --region=<region>
2) Route affected traffic to the previous model variant with fallback policy: set-route-priority --route=default --priority=stable
3) Notify SRE and Experiment Lead in #runtime-experiments and page runtime-oncall.
4) Capture full profiler snapshot and save to /artifacts/experiments/<id>/snapshot-<ts>.json
5) If GPU OOMs or watchdog trips observed, cordon nodes and escalate to infra (tag node with reason: experiment-rollback).

Post-rollback analysis (24–72 hours):
- Run reconstruction using captured traces and synthetic replay.
- Correlate kernel.exec_time spikes with dispatch.queue_depth and kvcache hit-rate.
- Produce a triage report: root cause, potential mitigations, and next steps.

Experiment types and recommended precautions:
- Kernel mapping changes (e.g., switching to fused attention kernel): low-latency risk; require synthetic replay with varied sequence-lengths and gating on p99.
- Scheduler policy changes (preemption thresholds, batch slicing): test in staging for queueing regressions. Use stress profiles with mixed-priority workloads.
- KV cache heuristics (eviction threshold, prefetch window): verify with long-running chat sessions and ensure session-affinity preserved.
- Quantization and mixed-precision rollouts: include correctness evaluation on unit prompt set and monitor token-level quality regressions.

Benchmarking and validation recipes (examples):
- Latency heatmap generation: replay 1M requests sampled from the last 7 days stratified by sequence length and model variant. Produce matrix: rows=seq_length_bins, cols=model_variants, cells=median/p99 latency.
- Cost-sensitivity sweep: run the same workload across model variants and quantization profiles, report per-token cost and normalized latency.
- Priority inversion stress test: create synthetic mix with 80% background low-priority requests and 20% high-priority short requests; measure high-priority p99 under kernel changes.

CLI examples and YAML manifests (for reproducibility):
- Feature flag example:
  {
    "flag": "kernel_experiment",
    "enabled": false,
    "scopes": ["staging", "canary-region-us-east-1"]
  }

- Canary rollout manifest (simplified):
  rollout: |
    - step: enable
      percent: 1
      wait: 30m
    - measure: latency_p99, error_rate
      threshold: {"p99_delta_ms": 20, "error_rate_delta": 0.005}
    - step: increase
      percent: 5
      wait: 2h

Data recording and artifacts to retain:
- Microbenchmark CSVs and raw traces (retain for 90 days).
- Profiler snapshots and GPU kernel timelines (retain for 365 days for variance analysis).
- Experiment ticket and final triage report (permanent).

Known issues and caveats (current):
- Intermittent kernel selection thrash: observed when multiple kernel hints exist for the same model/seq-length bin. Mitigation: add cooldown of 60s before switching kernel variant.
- Observability gaps for Private deployments: telemetry sampling rates are lower in some on-prem installs; include replay artifacts when operating in these environments.
- Quantized-execution correctness edge cases with long context windows (>16k): require guardrail tests and lower rollout percentage.

Runbook snippets for common alerts:
- Alert: kernel.exec_time.p99 spike
  1) Check dispatch.queue_depth and kvcache.hit_rate.
  2) If queue_depth elevated and kvcache hit_rate low, suspected warmup/eviction issue: trigger async kvcache prefetch for affected sessions.
  3) If dispatch backlog persists, enable emergency congestion-control: set-congestion-mode --level=throttle

- Alert: GPU occupancy drop with latency increase
  1) Validate kernel selection logs to see if a slower kernel was chosen.
  2) Roll back kernel selector or reduce concurrency on affected nodes.

Team wiki and experiment catalog guidance:
- Every experiment must have a short wiki page under /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/experiments/<experiment-id>. That page must include: hypothesis, bench reports, canary manifest, dashboards (links), artifact URIs, and final decision.
- Maintain an experiments index with metadata columns: id, title, owner, status, start_date, end_date, delta_p99_ms, delta_cost_pct, notes. Example CSV header: id,title,owner,status,start_date,end_date,delta_p99_ms,delta_cost_pct,notes

Release cadence and communication:
- Major kernel/scheduler changes should be communicated as part of the monthly runtime release notes with a short impact statement and links to the experiment pages.
- For high-impact internal rollouts, publish a pre-rollout note to #infra-announce with expected windows and rollback contact.

Appendix A: Example hypothesis (realistic)
- Hypothesis: Switching to fused-attention-v2 reduces p95 by 12% for sequence lengths 512-2048 with an expected per-token cost reduction of 6%, without increasing p99 by more than 10ms.
- Validation plan: microbench suite (3k synthetic samples across seq bins), staging canary 48h, production canary 5% for 24h.

Appendix B: Quick checklist (one-page)
- [ ] Hypothesis documented and reviewers assigned
- [ ] Telemetry instrumented and dashboard created
- [ ] Microbench reports attached
- [ ] Staging canary passed (24h)
- [ ] Production canary gates passed (30m, 3h, 24h)
- [ ] Post-rollout report published
